title: RBI and ECB Sign New MoU, Deepening India-EU Financial Ties
excerpt: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and ECB President Christine Lagarde ink an updated cooperation pact, replacing the decade-old 2015 agreement.
body:
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra and ECB President Christine Lagarde signed a landmark Memorandum of Understanding on Sunday, May 10, formally renewing the institutional relationship between two of the world's most consequential central banks.

**What They Signed:**
The agreement, announced simultaneously by both institutions, supersedes the previous MoU that dated to 2015. According to the official ECB press release, the updated pact 'provides a framework for a regular exchange of information, policy dialogue and technical cooperation' across areas of mutual interest in central banking.

**Why It Matters:**
Eleven years is a long time in global finance — the world has weathered a pandemic, a digital-payments revolution, and mounting geopolitical fragmentation since the last agreement. By refreshing the MoU now, both institutions signal a shared commitment to coordinated monetary governance at a moment when multilateral cooperation faces real pressure. ECB President Lagarde framed the signing plainly, saying it was 'important that we sustain global cooperation.' The pact gives the RBI a structured channel to align with European regulatory thinking on issues from cross-border settlements to emerging frameworks around digital currencies — areas where Indian and European policy is rapidly evolving.

**What to Watch:**
Follow whether the technical cooperation provisions translate into concrete joint initiatives — particularly on digital currency regulation and fintech oversight — as both the RBI and ECB accelerate their central bank digital currency programmes in the months ahead.
